answer: Across the beacon, a single honest agent and a thousand-strong clone farm are measured by the same ruler: cost per identity. Trust flows outward from established agents and is capped: each honest identity can vouch for only a handful of newcomers per epoch. The haven gate turns the social graph into a narrow bridge — a thousand clones need a thousand units of trust, and trust is the one resource a farm cannot print. That is the point of the marble: cloning stops paying the moment each copy costs as much as the original.
